blocks.text: Sets are fundamental to mathematics and computer science, forming the basis for understanding data structures, databases, and more. Let's explore the operations we can perform on sets.

blocks.markdown: A **set** is a collection of distinct objects, considered as an object in its own right. Sets are typically denoted by capital letters, such as $A$, $B$, or $C$. The objects in a set are called **elements** or **members**.

blocks.title: Set Notation
blocks.text: If $a$ is an element of set $A$, we write $a \in A$. If $a$ is not an element of $A$, we write $a \notin A$.

blocks.markdown: Common set operations include union, intersection, and complement. These operations allow us to combine or modify sets in various ways.

blocks.title: Union
blocks.text: The **union** of two sets $A$ and $B$, denoted $A \cup B$, is the set of elements that are in $A$, in $B$, or in both.

blocks.title: Intersection
blocks.text: The **intersection** of two sets $A$ and $B$, denoted $A \cap B$, is the set of elements that are in both $A$ and $B$.

blocks.title: Complement
blocks.text: The **complement** of a set $A$, denoted $A^c$, is the set of all elements not in $A$, relative to a universal set $U$.

blocks.latex: A \cup B = \{ x \mid x \in A \text{ or } x \in B \}
blocks.caption: Formal definition of union.

blocks.latex: A \cap B = \{ x \mid x \in A \text{ and } x \in B \}
blocks.caption: Formal definition of intersection.

blocks.title: Union and Intersection Example
blocks.prompt: Given sets $A = \{1, 2, 3\}$ and $B = \{2, 3, 4\}$, find $A \cup B$ and $A \cap B$.

steps.text: For $A \cup B$, combine all elements from $A$ and $B$ without repetition.
For $A \cap B$, find elements common to both $A$ and $B$.

blocks.title: Key Properties
blocks.text: Union and intersection are commutative and associative: $A \cup B = B \cup A$, $A \cap B = B \cap A$, $(A \cup B) \cup C = A \cup (B \cup C)$, $(A \cap B) \cap C = A \cap (B \cap C)$.

blocks.markdown: The **power set** of a set $A$, denoted $\mathcal{P}(A)$, is the set of all subsets of $A$. If $A$ has $n$ elements, then $\mathcal{P}(A)$ has $2^n$ elements.

steps.text: Include the empty set and $A$ itself.

blocks.title: Cartesian Product
blocks.text: The **Cartesian product** of two sets $A$ and $B$, denoted $A \times B$, is the set of all ordered pairs $(a, b)$ where $a \in A$ and $b \in B$.

rows: All ordered pairs from two sets
blocks.caption: Summary of set operations.

points: Sets are collections of distinct elements.
Union, intersection, and complement are basic set operations.
The power set contains all subsets of a set and has cardinality $2^n$ for a set with $n$ elements.
The Cartesian product forms ordered pairs from two sets.
